newsitem.title: USA: U.S. team to probe Russia's space station problems.
newsitem.headline: U.S. team to probe Russia's space station problems.

text.p: A team of U.S. experts will travel to Russia next month to evaluate problems with funding and delays of the key Russian components for the international space station, NASA chief Dan Goldin said on Wednesday.

In addition, Goldin said he would travel to Russia himself in April, and that both visits would be aimed at determining whether the problems on the Russian side are severe enough to warrant putting contingency plans for the space station into effect.
"Promises no longer count, it's action," Goldin told a House Appropriations panel.
Russian officials, including Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, have recently assured Washington that there will be enough money to complete their part of the project.

However, on Monday, Yuri Koptev, head of the Russian Space Agency, said the first Alpha module would be launched in June 1998, rather than November 1997, delaying the $40 billion project. A fire this week aboard the Russian space station Mir did little to bolster global confidence.

The new space station, to be complete by 2003, is being funded by Russia, the United States, the European Space Agency, Canada, Italy and Japan. Russia is building the first module, a cargo section, and the third, a service area where cosmonauts will live and work.

A delay in launching the first module will also delay launch of the second stage, a docking module being built in the United States. After the third module, other parts of the station will be attached in stages by 2003.

Goldin expressed doubts to the House panel that Russia would be able to deliver its modules on time, but said the National Aeronautics and Space Administration hopes to keep the "end date" of the project in place."

Contingency plans include the construction of an Interim Control Module, which would keep the embryonic station in proper orbit while waiting for the launch of the Russian service module, Goldin said.
